[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. No Child Left Behind (NCLB): Initially proposed by the Clinton administration in 1994, it mandated annual testing and accountability for schools receiving federal funding.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Race to the Top: Incentivized states to adopt education reform measures, such as high academic standards and tying teacher evaluations to student performance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Common Core State Standards: Aimed to establish consistent academic standards across states.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA): Replaced NCLB and gave states more control over education policy and assessment.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted successes of the Obama administration's policies, including Race to the Top and Common Core's positive impacts on student learning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned criticisms of NCLB for its focus on standardized testing and Race to the Top and Common Core for backlash from educators and parents.
